 # Data Model: Support Ticket Triage Assistant
 
 This feature is stateless: one ticket is processed per invocation and no application data is persisted. The shapes below describe runtime values and, where noted, human-owned evaluation data.
 
 ## Ticket
 
 | Field | Type | Constraints |
 |---|---|---|
 | `text` | `str` | Raw plain-text customer message; input is not trimmed. `text.strip() == ""` or `len(text) > 4000` is rejected before model setup. Python `len` counts Unicode code points. |
 
 The CLI starts from file bytes, decodes strict UTF-8 without newline translation, and removes exactly one leading U+FEFF before creating the ticket text. (FR-001–FR-003, FR-012–FR-013, GR-001)
 
 ## Triage decision
 
 A JSON object represented by a Python dictionary with exactly these six keys:
 
 | Key | Type / allowed values | Triage | Clarify | Refuse |
 |---|---|---|---|---|
 | `action` | string: `triage`, `clarify`, `refuse` | `triage` | `clarify` | `refuse` |
 | `category` | string: `billing`, `technical`, `account_access`, `shipping`, `other`; otherwise null | required | null | null |
 | `priority` | string: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `urgent`; otherwise null | required | null | null |
 | `summary` | string of 1–200 code points; otherwise null | required | null | null |
 | `clarification_question` | string of 5–200 code points ending in `?`; otherwise null | null | required | null |
 | `refusal_reason` | string: `invalid_input`, `prompt_injection`, `not_a_support_ticket`; otherwise null | null | null | required |
 
 Action and field presence/nullability must be consistent. Only the local deterministic guard can produce `invalid_input`; a model reply with that value is invalid. All output strings are checked for a 13-or-more ASCII digit run after spaces and hyphens are removed, an API-key-pattern match (`sk-` plus at least 20 ASCII alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen characters), and literal `OPENAI_API_KEY`. (FR-002, FR-004–FR-011; INV-001–INV-007; GR-002–GR-005)
 
 ## Model reply and errors
 
 | Entity | Fields / behavior |
 |---|---|
 | Model reply | Exact raw string returned by `ModelClient.complete(system, user)`. It must be strict JSON that parses into a valid decision; duplicates, constants such as `NaN`, extra/missing keys, malformed JSON, and any invariant violation invalidate it. |
 | `InvalidModelOutput` | Exception for every invalid raw reply. Its `raw_reply` attribute is the exact original string. Do not sanitize or rewrite this diagnostic value; CLI must never print it. |
 | `ServiceError` | Exception for service/configuration/network errors. The fixed message is exactly `Model service unavailable.` and it contains no underlying error, API key, or cause. |
 
 (FR-009–FR-011; INV-001–INV-007)
 
 ## Evaluation case and evaluation result (human-owned)
 
 These are specification-defined entities for `evals/` only; they do not imply creation or modification of evaluation files in this plan.
 
 | Entity | Required content and validation |
 |---|---|
 | Evaluation case | Unique id, input text, tags, gold action, and traces of applicable FR/INV/GR ids. Triage cases also include gold category, gold priority, and key terms. Refusal cases include gold refusal reason. `forbidden_terms`, if present, must be checked case-insensitively against every output string field. |
 | Per-case result | Case status and score. A contract/invariant/guardrail failure or wrong action yields `FAIL`, score 0. `InvalidModelOutput` is `FAIL`, one attempt, score 0, with independent Layers 1 and 2 run on its exact raw reply. A service failure after up to three attempts is `ERROR`, excluded from the aggregate. |
 | Evaluation run | Arithmetic mean of scored cases and final `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `INVALID`. Any `ERROR` makes the run `INVALID`. A `PASS` requires all contract/invariant checks, all guardrail cases passing, and aggregate score at least 0.85. |
 
 (FR-014–FR-019; EV-001–EV-004)
 
 ## Relationships and state
 
 `Ticket` → one `ModelClient` request (except deterministic guard refusals) → one raw `Model reply` → either one validated `Triage decision` or one explicit exception. There is no persisted state. The independent evaluator may process a dataset case once per run and may retry service failures up to two times, but retry policy does not belong to the library or OpenAI client.

 # Interface Contracts
 
 The public library and CLI are separate entry points over one service. The model protocol is injectable so callers and human-owned tests can control model replies without network access (NFR-001).
 
 ## Library
 
 ```text
 triage(ticket_text: str, client: ModelClient | None = None) -> dict
 ModelClient.complete(system: str, user: str) -> str
 ```
 
 - Check the deterministic guard first. Empty/whitespace-only or over-4000-code-point input returns the six-key `invalid_input` refusal with zero client creation, environment lookup, or model calls.
 - For other input, use the injected client or create `OpenAIClient`; send the fixed loaded system prompt and the exact ticket text as the user message.
 - Parse and validate the raw reply with the complete decision contract. Return validated values unchanged, or raise `InvalidModelOutput` with exact `raw_reply`.
 - Raise `ServiceError` for model configuration/service errors. Its message is exactly `Model service unavailable.`.
 
 ## Decision JSON object
 
 Every successful library result has exactly these keys: `action`, `category`, `priority`, `summary`, `clarification_question`, and `refusal_reason`. Types, enums, action-dependent nullability, code-point length rules, refusal provenance, and sensitive-pattern exclusions are defined in [data-model.md](../data-model.md) and the approved [specification](../spec.md) (FR-004–FR-011; INV-001–INV-007).
 
 The reply parser does not accept duplicate object keys (at any depth), non-standard JSON constants, non-object JSON, missing or extra keys, wrong types/enums, or any invariant violation. It performs no repair, inference, or normalization.
 
 ## OpenAI adapter
 
 `OpenAIClient.complete(system, user)`:
 
 1. Read `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL` at call time; strip only to determine whether each is missing/empty. If either is empty, raise `ServiceError` before network activity.
 2. Construct the official client with `api_key=...`, `timeout=30.0`, and `max_retries=0`.
 3. Call Chat Completions with one system message, one user message, and `response_format={"type":"json_object"}`. Do not set temperature or strict structured outputs.
 4. Return the response content string, or `""` if content is `None`.
 5. Catch only `openai.OpenAIError` and raise the fixed `ServiceError` with no chained underlying cause. Do not log, print, or expose credentials or SDK error text.
 
 The model itself must produce the JSON-object response specified in `prompts/system.md`; independent contract parsing remains mandatory.
 
 ## CLI
 
 ```text
 main(argv: list[str], client: ModelClient | None = None) -> int
 ```
 
 - Exactly one argument is required. Do not interpret options.
 - Read the named file as bytes; strict UTF-8 decode with no newline translation; remove one leading U+FEFF if present; then invoke `triage`.
 - Successful decisions, including refusals, are serialized as `json.dumps(decision, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)` encoded UTF-8, followed by exactly `b"\n"` on `sys.stdout.buffer`. Exit 0.
 - Failures write no stdout bytes and exactly one LF-terminated message to `sys.stderr.buffer`:
 
 | Condition | Exit | Stderr line |
 |---|---:|---|
 | Argument count is not one | 2 | `error: expected exactly one input file path` |
 | Missing, directory, unreadable file, or invalid UTF-8 | 2 | `error: cannot read input file` |
 | `ServiceError` | 3 | `error: model service unavailable` |
 | `InvalidModelOutput` | 4 | `error: model returned an invalid response` |
 
 The CLI must not print raw invalid replies or any partial/success-shaped JSON on error (FR-012–FR-013).
 
 ## Executable entry point and configuration
 
 `env_loader.py` exposes exactly one public function:
 
 ```text
 load_env(path: pathlib.Path) -> None
 ```
 
 It reads `path` as UTF-8 and returns silently if the file is missing or unreadable. For each line, it strips surrounding whitespace and skips blank lines, lines starting with `#`, and lines without `=`. Otherwise it splits at the first `=`, strips whitespace around both the name and value, and sets `os.environ[name] = value` only when the name is nonempty and not already in `os.environ`. It never prints or logs anything and never raises for a malformed line.
 
 `__main__.py` imports `cli.main` and `env_loader.load_env`, calls `load_env(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / ".env")` to locate `.env` in the Part-1B project root (the parent of `src`), then raises `SystemExit(cli.main(sys.argv[1:]))`. It contains no other logic and catches no exceptions. The library modules never read `.env`. The plan has not opened or read any `.env` file. Only `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL` are consumed by the OpenAI adapter.

 # Implementation Plan: Support Ticket Triage Assistant
 
 **Branch**: `001-support-ticket-triage` | **Date**: 2026-11-03 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
 
 **Input**: Approved feature specification and implementation constraints supplied for this plan.
 
 ## Summary
 
 Build a Python 3.12+ library and one-file command-line tool that turn a single customer ticket into a validated six-field triage decision. A deterministic guard handles empty, whitespace-only, and over-limit text before any model configuration or network access. Other tickets are sent unchanged as user data alongside one invariant system prompt to an injectable model client. The raw JSON reply is strictly parsed and validated; invalid output and service failures remain distinct, sanitized errors. The CLI handles strict UTF-8 file input and byte-exact output. The official `openai` package is the sole third-party runtime dependency. See [research.md](./research.md) for decisions and [contracts/interfaces.md](./contracts/interfaces.md) for public interfaces.
 
 ## Technical Context
 
 **Language/Version**: Python 3.12+
 
 **Primary Dependencies**: Official `openai` Python package only at runtime; standard library for all other runtime behavior.
 
 **Storage**: None. Input is one file for the CLI; no application persistence.
 
 **Testing**: Human-owned tests and evaluation components specified in the approved spec. `tests/`, `evals/`, and `.harness/` are not generated or modified by this plan.
 
 **Target Platform**: Python 3.12+ environments with access to the configured OpenAI service when model-assisted triage is required.
 
 **Project Type**: Python library plus command-line interface.
 
 **Performance Goals**: No latency or throughput target is specified. The OpenAI client timeout is 30 seconds; deterministic checks are local.
 
 **Constraints**: Exactly one third-party runtime dependency; fixed six-key contract; Unicode code-point length counting; no response repair; sanitized service errors; no output of specified sensitive patterns; the system prompt is identical for each ticket. No project/dependency manifest, tests, evals, or harness files are in scope. `.env` files must not be opened or read during this planning task.
 
 **Scale/Scope**: One ticket per library or CLI invocation; no history, persistence, attachments, UI, or multi-ticket processing.
 
 ## Constitution Check
 
 ### Pre-design gate
 
 | Principle / constraint | Plan decision | Status |
 |---|---|---|
 | I. Modular boundaries and secret isolation | Separate guard, prompt loading, model protocol/client, contract parsing, service orchestration, CLI, and optional `__main__` environment loading. Only `openai_client.py` reads model credentials and performs network activity. | PASS |
 | II. Untrusted input and deterministic guardrails | Treat the user message strictly as ticket data; reject invalid length/blank input before client creation or environment access. | PASS |
 | III. Validated contract and explicit failures | Validate every raw reply without normalization; distinguish `InvalidModelOutput` from fixed-message `ServiceError`. | PASS |
 | IV. Independent evaluation and acceptance | Keep the human-owned evaluation harness independent; map every AC in [acceptance-traceability.md](./contracts/acceptance-traceability.md). Do not produce or change evaluation files. | PASS |
 | V. Minimal dependencies and maintainability | Python 3.12+, official `openai` package only at runtime, otherwise standard library; use direct, small modules. | PASS |
 | Evaluation and scope controls | Do not create or alter `tests/`, `evals/`, or `.harness/`; no change to thresholds or harness behavior. | PASS |
 
 No violations or complexity exceptions are required.
 
 ### Post-design gate
 
 The proposed package and prompt tree preserves the boundaries and constraints above. Runtime secrets remain isolated to the OpenAI client; deterministic input refusals need no configuration. Evaluation traces are documentation only and point to human-owned components. The generated plan artifacts stay under `specs/001-support-ticket-triage/`. **Result: PASS; no unresolved clarifications.**
 
 ## Architecture and Key Decisions
 
 1. **Small, injectable module boundaries**: `guard.py` performs deterministic input validation; `contract.py` is pure parsing and invariant validation; `model_client.py` defines the replaceable protocol; `openai_client.py` owns environment reads and network access; `service.py` composes them; `cli.py` owns argument, file, and stream behavior. This satisfies Constitution I and V, NFR-001, FR-001–FR-002, FR-009–FR-013, and INV-001–INV-007.
 2. **Input gate precedes all external state**: The service checks exactly `text.strip() == ""` or `len(text) > 4000` without trimming the original ticket. It returns the deterministic `invalid_input` decision without creating a default client or reading environment configuration. This implements FR-002, FR-008, GR-001, and AC-001–AC-004/AC-045.
 3. **Fixed prompt and untrusted user message**: Load `prompts/system.md` relative to the package location and send it unchanged for each call; pass the exact ticket text only as the user message.  All requirements supplied for this feature are sufficiently specific; there are no unresolved technical-context questions. This research records the fixed decisions and the relevant SDK integration guidance. It does not change the approved specification.
 
 ## Python runtime and dependency boundary
 
 **Decision**: Use Python 3.12+ and the official `openai` package as the only third-party runtime dependency. Use the standard library for JSON handling, regular expressions, environment access, file I/O, and CLI serialization.
 
 **Rationale**: The runtime version and dependency boundary are explicit in the feature input and constitution (V). Separating the dependency behind `ModelClient` allows deterministic tests and avoids requiring network access for library tests (NFR-001).
 
 **Alternatives considered**: Third-party schema, CLI, retry, and dotenv libraries were not selected because the contract and behavior are fully defined and the dependency budget excludes them. No package or requirements manifest is in scope.
 
 ## OpenAI client integration
 
 **Decision**: Implement `OpenAIClient.complete()` with the official SDK's `OpenAI` client, configured at call time with `api_key`, `timeout=30.0`, and `max_retries=0`. Use Chat Completions with a system message and exact ticket user message, plus `response_format={"type":"json_object"}`. Do not send a temperature parameter and do not request strict structured outputs. Map only `openai.OpenAIError` to `ServiceError` using `raise ... from None`; do not log or expose the original exception. Return an empty string when the response message content is `None`.
 
 **Rationale**: These request parameters and error semantics are fixed by the feature input and implement FR-003, FR-009–FR-010, and AC-019–AC-020/AC-050–AC-051.  **Alternatives considered**: Responses API and strict structured outputs are not selected because the requested interface explicitly requires Chat Completions and JSON mode without strict outputs.  - [openai-python README: supported Python and Chat Completions](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/README.md)
 - [openai-python README: retries and timeouts](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/README.md#retries)

     if len(argv) != 1:
